payload.claim: The spec's own "Linux `flock` is not measured" note discloses that two kernel-level properties the fix depends on — that an `flock` belongs to one open file description, so a second `open()` of the same path within one process conflicts with its own first lock (used by the second criterion's witness to simulate a same-process contender), and that a lock is freed once every descriptor on that description closes, so SIGKILL frees it (used by the first criterion's witness) — were verified only on macOS, never on the Linux host the acceptance witnesses would actually run on if the cell's own test loop runs on Linux. The documented Linux `flock(2)` semantics do match what's assumed, so this is not a blocker, but it is a platform assumption a person should sign off on before a cell starts spending.
